lessons.title: തിങ്കൾ to ഞായർ — the week Malayalam shares with Tamil
lessons.headword: തിങ്കൾ ചൊവ്വ ബുധൻ വ്യാഴം വെള്ളി ശനി ഞായർ
lessons.gloss: the seven weekdays — Malayalam shares Tamil's native planet-words, being its closest cousin

needs: your eyes for one table that cannot be read aloud
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes for one table that cannot be read aloud. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called You'll want to know until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Malayalam and Tamil are close cousins — they were once, long ago, the same language — and nowhere does that show more clearly than in the words for the days of the week.

There is a table here I cannot read to you — 4 columns and 7 rows, and it has more columns than can be held in the ear at once. Its columns are: Malayalam, planet-word, meaning, compare Tamil. Come back and look at it when you have stopped.

This is the closest family match anywhere in Dravidian: thiṅkaḷ/thiṅgaḷ, veḷḷi/veḷḷi, and ñāyar/ñāyiṟu are essentially the same words, because Malayalam only became a distinct language from Tamil within roughly the last thousand years or so. Where Tamil says கிழமை (kizhamai) for "day," Malayalam says ஆழ்ச (āzhcha) — a different word for the same idea (the two aren't confirmed cognates; treat this as two languages solving the same naming problem separately, not necessarily one shared root). Like Tamil, Malayalam mixes native planet-words (Moon, Mars, Venus, Sun) with Sanskrit ones (Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn) — the same split, inherited from the same shared ancestor language.

segments.instruction: the shared words — "veḷḷi" (Venus), same in both Malayalam and Tamil

segments.instruction: the Sanskrit ones — "budhan, vyāzham, śani" — Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the Sanskrit ones — "budhan, vyāzham, śani" — Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn]

segments.text: Why do Malayalam and Tamil's day-names look so alike? (They were the same language until roughly a thousand years ago.) Which planet-names does Malayalam share almost word-for-word with Tamil? (thiṅkaḷ/Moon, veḷḷi/Venus, ñāyar/Sun — and covva/Mars, a worn variant of cevvāy.) Which three come from Sanskrit in both languages? (Mercury (Budha), Jupiter (vyāzham/viyāzhaṉ), Saturn (Śani).)
